summary: Creates the missing IANA registry for ICE options, which RFC 5245 on Interactive Connectivity Establishment lacked, and updates that RFC. It was replaced by RFC 8839.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6336 creates an IANA registry for ICE option identifiers. It sets rules for their names and the information a registration request must include.

how do i register an ice option

subtitle: Creates the IANA registry for Interactive Connectivity Establishment options.

tldr.problem: RFC 5245 defined ICE options for signaling extension support but did not establish an IANA registry for them.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6336 creates an ICE Options registry and specifies the syntax, registration policy, and information required for a request.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6336 updates RFC 5245 and was obsoleted by RFC 8839.

today: RFC 6336 was obsoleted by RFC 8839 and updates RFC 5245, according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: The Missing ICE Registry
sections.content: RFC 5245 defines ICE options that an agent can include in signaling to identify supported ICE extensions. RFC 6336 explains that no IANA registry had been created for these option identifiers. A registry helps prevent conflicts as extension specifications add options.
sections.plainLanguage: ICE agents use option identifiers to signal support for extensions. This RFC creates a registry to keep those identifiers coordinated.

sections.title: Option Syntax and Registration
sections.content: An ICE option identifier follows the ice-option-tag syntax in RFC 5245, using letters, digits, plus signs, or slashes. The syntax permits any length, though the RFC recommends no more than 20 characters. Registration uses Specification Required and must include the identifier, contact details, change-control information, a short description, and references to the specification.
sections.plainLanguage: An option name can use letters, digits, plus, and slash. A registration request must explain the option and identify who is responsible for it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RFC 6336 says it defines an IANA registry for an existing concept and introduces no new security considerations. The document itself registers no ICE option.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC creates the registry but adds no option. It says the registry definition introduces no new security considerations.
